changes.replacement: The remaining witness values are whatever else the prover supplies to satisfy the constraints. Zero-knowledge keeps them out of the proof. They stay hidden only to the extent that they cannot be reconstructed from public data, and zero-knowledge does not make a transition private. The statement bytes, the proof-claim outputs, the settlement transaction and its actual outputs are all visible on the ledger. A public evidence bundle, as proposed, would leave out witness values, private keys and setup secrets.

changes.expected: The design is safe but not guaranteed to make progress. Any catalogue account can Revoke, which advances the sequence, and a competing settlement can spend the same state first. Either event leaves the issued claims pointing at a stale target. Those claims cannot settle and stay locked until the claimant's chosen expiry. Someone can copy a proof and re-issue it with the same claimant and a new expiry, but only that claimant can release it. An envelope with the wrong claimant can be minted but cannot settle.
changes.replacement: Any catalogue account can Revoke, which advances the sequence, and a competing settlement can spend the same state first. Either event leaves the issued claims pointing at a stale target. Those claims cannot settle and stay locked until the claimant's chosen expiry. Someone can copy a proof and re-issue it with the same claimant and a new expiry, but only that claimant can release it. An envelope with the wrong claimant can be minted but cannot settle.
